//generated: Which paths nobody types. The Review tab opens with a band naming every commit that
landed AFTER the agent's review commit — the one thing a page built from a diff
cannot see, because every number on it was measured before those commits existed.
The band is RED when a file outside this list moved and GREY when they all match it:
a regenerated diagram, a spec rewritten by a pre-commit hook or a redrawn .drawio is
not somebody editing the change under review, and a band that is red for those is a
band nobody reads by the third branch.
Leave it out and the defaults below apply. Writing it REPLACES them: a project that
says what it generates has said it. `*` stops at a slash, `**` crosses them, and a
leading `**/` is optional, so `**/generated/**` covers a top-level generated/ too.

drawio.//redraw: The repository's own patch script: what draws a concept or a link the
drawio.//redraw2: code has and the map lacks, in red, as a to-do. Named here and never
drawio.//redraw3: guessed — the page turns it into a button that rewrites a checked-in
drawio.//redraw4: file. Leave it out and the page offers no way to start over.
drawio.name: conceptual

sequence.//: The traced suites, whose output is COMMITTED (generated/*.genseq.puml) — which
sequence.//2: is why `app` matters more here than it does for the film. A run that reached
sequence.//3: another checkout listening on the same port does not fail: it draws that
sequence.//4: checkout's code, under this branch's name, and the pictures go into the
sequence.//6: `app` is the same block `video.app` is — `up` prints the URL, `down` runs in a
sequence.//7: finally, {sha}/{shortsha} come from git — or the word "video" to borrow that
sequence.//8: block rather than repeat it. Borrowing is never implicit: a stack that is right
sequence.//9: for a film is not automatically right for a suite that needs a trace collector
sequence.//10: behind it, and THIS project's does — its containers carry no OTLP endpoint and
sequence.//11: no Java agent, so the stack these commands need is still the ./start-*.sh one,
sequence.//12: started by hand in the documented order (grafana BEFORE backend). With no
sequence.//13: `app`, the step runs against whatever is listening and says what was missing
sequence.//14: if the suite could not run.
sequence.//15: `app.env` names the variables the suites read; the default is BASE_URL and
sequence.//16: API_URL, and this project's Playwright/Cucumber glue reads API_BASE_URL.
commands: cd petclinic-test && GENSEQ_REFRESH=1 npm run trace:diagram

c2.//: The C4 container view, PROJECTED from the sequence diagrams the step above
c2.//2: draws — nothing here is a drawing. It lands as the last diagram on the
c2.//3: Structure tab. Every key is optional: with no `c2` block at all it is still
c2.//4: built, from the lifelines and the arrows alone.
c2.//5: `containers` corrects the only thing a sequence diagram cannot say — what
c2.//6: KIND of thing a lifeline is — and names the stack, which is never guessed.
c2.//7: `kind` is one of container, db, queue, person, external.
c2.//8: `as` folds two lifelines into one container, for a suite that renamed its
c2.//9: own participant; `drop` keeps one out of the picture entirely, which is
c2.//10: what a test harness needs: a C2 shows what is DEPLOYED, and a MockMvc test
c2.//11: is deployed nowhere. A Playwright suite is the opposite and stays — but
c2.//12: name the box after what SHIPS (the browser running the app), not after the
c2.//13: harness that drives it in CI.
c2.//14: `sources` defaults to **/*.genseq.puml, outside target/ and node_modules/.
c2.//15: `name` is the card's title on the page and the stem of the files it
c2.//16: writes, and it is a VIEW KEY, not a level: `C2` on its own names the
c2.//17: level in the C4 model the way `C3` does, and a card titled with it says
c2.//18: which shelf the picture came off rather than what is on it. A project
c2.//19: whose C4 lives in a Structurizr DSL already has the key — petclinic's
c2.//21: C2-Containers.puml — so spell it the same and get one name for one
c2.//22: picture across the model, the export and this page. Defaults to
c2.//23: C2-Containers, which is that same convention for a project with no DSL.
c2.name: C2-Containers

city.//: `tests` runs before the city is drawn: its CRAP and coverage colours need a
city.//2: JaCoCo report, and -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true is what makes the report
city.//3: goal run at all when a test fails. Without it Maven aborts in the test phase
city.//4: and the city is coloured from whatever stale report was left on disk.
city.//5: `baseline` is the coverage the default branch measured and committed; the
city.//6: page reads it out of git at the diff's base ref to draw the before/after of
city.//7: coverage and CRAP, with no second checkout and no second test run. Refresh it
city.//8: only on the default branch: regenerate-codecity.sh --write-baseline.
city.//9: `tests` may be a list: measuring a browser suite separately takes the unit
city.//10: run, the acceptance run against a separately started app, and a merge of
city.//11: their two .exec files into the two reports the city colours by.
tests: cd petclinic-test && JACOCO_E2E=1 PW_TRACE=on npm test
cd petclinic-backend && mvn -o -q jacoco:merge@merge-all jacoco:report@report-all jacoco:report@report-acceptance
city.title: Code City

traces.//: Playwright's own recordings of the run, carried onto the page so a reviewer
traces.//2: can step through what each test did — every action with the page either side
traces.//3: of it, the console and the network — without checking the branch out.
traces.//4: `report` is the html reporter's output directory. Nothing is run from here:
traces.//5: the suite `city.tests` already ran is the one harvested, which is why that
traces.//6: command turns tracing ON (PW_TRACE=on above, read by playwright.config.ts).
traces.//7: A project with no other run to attach to puts its own `commands` here.
traces.//8: `limit` caps how many travel with the page, failures first — they are
traces.//9: megabytes each and the page is offered as a downloadable zip. What is left
traces.//10: behind is counted on the page rather than quietly dropped.
traces.//11: `cucumber`: scenarios run by cucumber-js, which writes no Playwright report.
traces.//12: The project's own hooks record one zip + sidecar JSON per scenario there
traces.//13: (see reference/content-schema.md, traces); leave it out if there are none.

video.//: The film of the feature working. `out` is where it lands; `app` is how the
video.//2: run gets the application it is filmed against, and it is the important half.
video.//3: Without `app` the recorder only checks that SOMETHING answers on BASE_URL
video.//4: and API_URL (:4200 / :8080 by default) — which is a test of the port, not of
video.//5: the commit. This machine keeps several checkouts of one repository and any
video.//6: of them can serve :4200, so on 17 Sep 2026 a review of `test-pr` shipped a
video.//7: film of `main`: the narration came from this branch's diff and the frames
video.//8: from another branch, and every caption asserted what the picture denied.
video.//9: With `app`, the run owns its instance. `up` builds the commit under review
video.//10: into containers of its own and prints the host port it got; `url` asks for
video.//11: that port again; `down` runs in a finally, so a crashed film leaves nothing
video.//12: behind. `{sha}` and `{shortsha}` are filled from `git rev-parse HEAD` — never
video.//13: written here, or they would be right until the next push. The URL is
video.//14: exported as BOTH BASE_URL and API_URL: the container's nginx proxies /api/
video.//15: on its own origin, and two different values is how a film drives one
video.//16: instance's screens against another instance's data.

//complexity: Nothing to configure: with no `complexity` key at all, the step reads both sides
itself out of the Java sources (endpoint-complexity.py), the baseline straight from
the merge-base. Configure it only to override that with a measurement the project
already makes — `extract` is a command that writes the two snapshots, `before` and
`after` are where they land, in the schema endpoint-complexity-delta.py reads:
[{kind, httpMethod, path, handler, flowCc, flow:[{method, cognitive}]}, ...].

dsaudit.//: Two RUNNING builds, side by side: this branch, and the merge-base. It is the
dsaudit.//2: only step that needs both sides of the branch up at the same time, and that
dsaudit.//3: is why it is the only step with TWO instances to its name.
dsaudit.//4: `app` is the same block `video.app` is — "video" borrows it rather than
dsaudit.//5: repeating it — and the step expands it twice: once with HEAD's {sha}/
dsaudit.//6: {shortsha}, once with the merge-base's. Both host ports are read back out of
dsaudit.//7: what each `up` printed (they are ephemeral on purpose: that is what lets two
dsaudit.//8: builds of one repository be up together), and both instances come `down` in
dsaudit.//9: a finally, including when only one of the two ever came up.
dsaudit.//10: Drop `app` and name `base-new`/`base-old` instead if the project keeps two
dsaudit.//11: builds served by hand. run-steps.py then probes both before starting the
dsaudit.//12: browser and skips the step naming the URL that did not answer — which is
dsaudit.//13: what this file said until 19 Sep 2026, when it emerged that naming two
dsaudit.//14: ports nobody starts means the step is skipped on every single run and the
dsaudit.//15: UX tab arrives empty, explaining that it is empty.
dsaudit.//screens: EVERY screen of the app, deep-linked to a seeded row, not the ones
dsaudit.//screens2: somebody guessed the branch touched. The audit shoots them all and
dsaudit.//screens3: draws only those whose DOM changed; the rest are named in one line.
dsaudit.//screens4: run-steps.py follows every changed component to its route and flags,
dsaudit.//screens5: in red on the page, any route this list does not reach.
